title: Minimum edges for graph dimension d in general

problemStatement.formal: What is minEdges(d), the minimum number of edges in a graph of dimension exactly d?
problemStatement.plain: Study the function minEdges(d) giving the minimum number of edges needed for a graph to have unit-distance dimension exactly d. Known: minEdges(d) = C(d+1,2) for d ≤ 3 and d = 5, but minEdges(4) = 9 < C(5,2) = 10.
whyMatters: Connects combinatorial graph theory to Euclidean geometry
The d=4 exception reveals unexpected structure in unit-distance graphs
Understanding minEdges(d) characterizes the edge-dimension trade-off

open: Is K_{d+1} optimal for all d ≠ 4?
knownResults.goal: Determine the asymptotic behavior of minEdges(d)

insights: The simplex embedding v_i = (1/√2)e_i places K_n in ℝⁿ with unit distances
The deficiency δ(d) = C(d+1,2) - minEdges(d) cleanly captures the d=4 anomaly
Complete graph optimality conjecture is equivalent to δ(d) = 0 for d ≠ 4
The optimality conjecture implies monotonicity via C(d+1,2) monotonicity + d=4 case handling
Under optimality, successive differences Δ(d) = d+1, which is the binomial increment
d=4 is formally verified as the unique anomaly for d ≤ 5
